title: Register content library items on vCenter so an interrupted create can be retried without duplicating it
prompt:
Platform automation ticket for our VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 estate. The job that seeds our workload-domain content libraries ran twice last night after vCenter dropped a response mid-create, and we ended up with duplicate library items that the image-management team then had to unpick by hand. Rebuild the job so a retry can never create the same item twice.

Implement `VcfLibraryItemRegistration.psm1` at the workspace root. It registers a set of named items in a local content library on a vCenter, creating only the ones that are missing, and it survives vCenter answering a create with `503` after the item has already been committed.

The runner installs `VMware.Sdk.vSphere.ContentLibrary` 9.0.0.24798382 and its dependencies. Import that genuine PowerCLI SDK module and build every request body with its model initializers: `Initialize-ContentLibraryFindSpec`, `Initialize-ContentLibraryItemFindSpec`, and `Initialize-ContentLibraryItemModel`. Do not vendor VMware modules into the repository.

The protected `docs/contract.json` is a projection of `specifications/vsphere/openapi/automation/vcenter.yaml` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at the commit recorded in `docs/official_sources.json`. It comes from the specification rather than a documentation page, and it is pinned to the `9.0.0.0` tag, not the `9.1.0.0` revision of the same file. The only operationIds in scope are `Cis.Session_create`, `Content.Library_find`, `Content.Library.Item_find`, `Content.Library.Item_create`, and `Content.Library.Item_get`; nothing else is served. Every path in the contract is reached under the `/api` base path the specification declares.

The acceptance harness calls:

`Invoke-VcfLibraryItemRegistration -Server <string> -Credential <pscredential> -LibraryName <string> -Item <object[]> [-MaxAttempts <int>] [-SleepAction <scriptblock>]`

Requirements:

- Export only `Invoke-VcfLibraryItemRegistration`. `-Server` is the vCenter base URL. Each `-Item` element carries a `Name` and an optional `Type`. `MaxAttempts` defaults to 3. When `SleepAction` is supplied, invoke it with the delay in seconds instead of calling `Start-Sleep`.
- Open one session for the whole run with `Cis.Session_create`. It declares no request body: the credentials travel in an HTTP Basic `Authorization` header and the session token comes back as a bare JSON string. Carry that token in the `vmware-api-session-id` header on every later call, and stop sending `Authorization` once the session exists.
- Resolve the library with a single `Content.Library_find` whose `Content.Library.FindSpec` sets `name` to the requested library and `type` to `LOCAL`, and nothing else. Fail rather than guess if the search does not match exactly one library.
- For each requested item, ask `Content.Library.Item_find` first, with a `Content.Library.Item.FindSpec` that sets `library_id` and `name` and nothing else. An item that already exists is recorded as found and is never created again.
- Create the missing items with `Content.Library.Item_create`. The `Content.Library.ItemModel` on the wire carries `library_id`, `name`, and `type` only when the caller supplied one. An optional member the caller never set must be absent from the body, never sent as null, as an empty string, or as an empty object; note that the SDK model initializers keep unset members on the object and their `ToJson()` renders them as null, and that the wire member names are the snake_case names in the contract rather than the PascalCase property names on the model.
- `Content.Library.Item_create` takes a `Client-Token` request header holding a UUID, and that header is what makes the call retryable: vCenter records the token against the item it creates, so a create replayed with the same token returns the item that already exists instead of creating a second one. Mint one token per item before its first attempt and replay it unchanged on every retry of that item. A retry that mints a fresh token is a new creation request and vCenter rejects it with `400` `Vapi.Std.Errors.AlreadyExists` once the first attempt has committed. Send `Client-Token` on no other operation.
- One create will be answered with `503` after vCenter has already committed the item, which is what a lost response looks like from the client. Retry the create itself up to `MaxAttempts`; do not fall back to re-running the find to recover, and do not retry a `4xx` — those are terminal.
- Read each registered item back with `Content.Library.Item_get` on its identifier.
- Return an object exposing `LibraryId` and `Items`, where `Items` holds one entry per requested item in the requested order, each exposing `Name`, `ItemId`, and `Created`.

Acceptance: `pwsh -NoProfile -File verify.ps1`. It starts contract-pinned loopback vCenter fixtures on `127.0.0.1`, drives the module with dummy credentials, and reads their request logs to check the exact method, target, query string, body member set, session-token discipline, `Client-Token` reuse across the retry, omission of every unset optional member, retry ceiling, injected delays, and terminal `4xx` handling. No live VMware endpoint is contacted. `verify.ps1`, `mock_vcenter.py`, `.gitignore`, and everything under `docs/` are protected; do not modify them.
